rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Continuity in the calculus unit is the **three-part test plus the full species atlas**. The test — value, limit, agreement — has three failure modes, but the "limit does not exist" branch splits graphically: **removable** (open or detached dot; repair f(a) = L), **jump** (finite unequal sides; vertical gap), **infinite** (±∞ side; vertical asymptote, odd multiplicity splitting, even unifying), and the fourth species…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - continuity: f(a) = lim_{x→a} f(x), both existing - species: removable / jump / infinite / oscillatory - rational triage: shared zeros → holes; survivors → walls

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ answer with no steps → ✅ show each step and box the result.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ indeterminate forms 0/0, ∞/∞, 0·∞ → l'hôpital: lim f/g = lim f'/g' (when applicable)..

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Continuous at a iff f(a) = lim_{x->a} f(x) with both existing; the species are removable, jump, infinite, oscillatory."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The folding graph*** - sin(1/x) near 0 crosses zero infinitely often between any point and the origin: no side limit, no repair, a genuinely wild species.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Continuity and Its Graphs The calculus-unit continuity canonical: the three-part test, the **discontinuity taxonomy with graphs**, and the classification workflow — now with the graphical gallery as the centrepiece.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Continuity at a point and on intervals - **Three-part test:** f(a) exists; lim_{x→a} f(x) exists; f(a) = lim. Continuous on an interval ⟺ continuous at every interior point + one-sided at endpoints. - **Closure families:** polynomials (ℝ), rational (q ≠ 0), roots (domain), sin/cos (ℝ), eˣ (ℝ), ln x (x > 0); sums/products/quotients/compositions inherit.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Domain, closure, triage, report. Graph features map to test parts: open dot = hole, gap = jump, asymptote = wall, folding = oscillator.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The three-part test has three failure modes, but the limit-failure splits graphically into jump, wall and oscillator - four species, one test.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Three-part test: f(a) exists, limit exists, equality; intervals add one-sided endpoints. Closure families certify whole intervals. Discontinuity taxonomy: removable (limit exists, value missing/wrong - open or detached dot, repair f(a) = L), jump (finite unequal sides - vertical gap, non-removable), infinite (side…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Circuit diagrams mark breaks like discontinuity graphs: open dots (holes), gaps (switches/jumps), and short-to-ground spikes (walls).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Sketch and classify g(x) = sin(1/x) for x ≠ 0 with g(0) = 0.** — **Behaviour near 0:** as x → 0⁺ (or 0⁻), 1/x → +∞ (or −∞), and sin(1/x) sweeps the full range [−1, 1] infinitely many times — between any two points near 0 the function crosses 0, 1 and −1 repeatedly.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the constants a and b so that f is continuous on ℝ, where f(x) = ax + b for x ≤ 1, f(x) = x² + 1 for 1 < x < 3, and f(x) = 3x − a − b for x ≥ 3.** — **Seam 1 (x = 1):** LHL = a(1) + b = a + b; RHL = 1² + 1 = 2; f(1) = a + b. Continuity ⟹ **a + b = 2**.…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): Show that the equation x³ + x − 1 = 0 has exactly one real root, located in (0, 1).** — **Existence (IVT):** f(x) = x³ + x − 1 is a polynomial ⟹ continuous on [0, 1]; f(0) = −1 < 0 and f(1) = 1 > 0 ⟹ by the Intermediate Value Theorem a root exists in (0, 1).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Graph signature | |---|---|---| | **Removable** | Limit exists, value off | open/detached dot | | **Jump** | Sides finite, unequal | vertical gap | | **Infinite** | Side blow-up | vertical asymptote | | **Oscillatory** | No side limit | infinite folding |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the taxonomy has four species - The three-part test has exactly three failure modes, but "limit does not exist" splits into two graphically distinct ways — finite disagreement (jump) and unboundedness (infinite) — plus the no-limit-at-all case (oscillation). Four species, one test.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Species atlas** | Species | Sides | f(a) | Repair | |---|---|---|---| | removable | equal finite | missing/wrong | f(a) := L | | jump | finite ≠ | any | none | | infinite | ±∞ | any | none | | oscillatory | DNE | any | none |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A removable discontinuity can be "fixed" by redefining the function at one point. Jump and infinite discontinuities cannot be removed this way.  ·  The function $f(x) = \sin(1/x)$ for $x \neq 0$ and $f(0) = 0$ has an essential discontinuity at $x = 0$ — no matter how you define $f(0)$, the limit does not exist.  ·  A vertical asymptote always indicates an infinite discontinuity, but not all discontinuities involve vertical asymptotes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A function can be continuous at a point but not differentiable there (e.g., $f(x) = |x|$ at $x = 0$). Continuity is a weaker condition than differentiability.  ·  A function can have a limit at a point without being continuous there — the function might be undefined at that point, or its value might differ from the limit.  ·  Verified PYQ: NEB 2024 continuity definition + x^2 at x = 1 check - assigned to this row. Other items NEB-style practice.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Compare f₁(x) = sin(1/x) (f₁(0) = 0), f₂(x) = x·sin(1/x) (f₂(0) = 0) and f₃(x) = x²·sin(1/x) (f₃(0) = 0) at x = 0.** — **f₁:** sin(1/x) oscillates in [−1, 1] infinitely often near 0 with **no damping** ⟹ no one-sided limit ⟹ **oscillatory discontinuity** at 0.…  ·  **NEB-style (4m): State the Intermediate Value Theorem and use it to show that f(x) = x − cos x has a root between 0 and π/2.** — **Theorem:** if f is continuous on the closed interval [a, b] and u lies between f(a) and f(b), then some c ∈ (a, b) satisfies f(c) = u.…  ·  Define continuity at x = a and check x² at x = 1.

rows.text: Classify the breaks of (x + 1)/(x² − 1) with graph features.  ·  Classify sin(1/x) (g(0) = 0) at 0.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: indeterminate forms 0/0, ∞/∞, 0·∞ → l'hôpital: lim f/g = lim f'/g' (when applicable).  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Discontinuous" ≠ "the limit DNE":** a removable break has a perfectly good limit — only the value is wrong.  ·  **One-sided continuity at jumps:** f can be right-continuous at a jump (Heaviside) — discontinuity and one-sided continuity coexist.
